compatibility.title: Which Subaru Models Use the FB25?
compatibility.intro: The FB25 is Subaru's larger-capacity naturally aspirated boxer engine, introduced in 2010 and progressively replacing the EJ253 across the range. It is the engine of choice for Subaru's larger models where the FB20's 2.0-litre displacement would be insufficient.

failures.title: Subaru FB25 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails
failures.goodYearsLine: The FB25 improved significantly over its production run. The pre-2018 FB25A/B used port injection and was more prone to oil consumption. The 2018+ FB25D introduced direct injection, higher compression (12.0:1 vs 10.0:1) and improved power output, but oil consumption and cam carrier leaks remain concerns. Unlike the EJ25 it replaced, the FB25 does NOT have the notorious head gasket failure reputation - that issue was largely fixed with this engine generation.

variants.title: FB25 Variants - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: While FB25 is the family name, there are three primary variants - the early FB25A, the mid-production FB25B, and the later direct-injection FB25D. The differences matter when buying a replacement. ### FB25A - 2010-2012 (early port injection) - Fitted to: Subaru Forester SH (2010-2012), Subaru Legacy BM (2010-2012) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Port injection. Compression ratio: 10.0:1. Power: 169 hp (126 kW) at 5,800 rpm, 235 Nm at 4,100 rpm. Dual AVCS (variable intake and exhaust valve timing). Timing chain (no belt). - Sub-code-specific failure note: Oil consumption is the primary issue on this variant - early engines are more prone to piston ring wear. - Interchange note: Direct swap with FB25B is generally possible, but check ECU compatibility. Not compatible with FB25D without significant changes. ### FB25B - 2012-2018 (port injection, revised) - Fitted to: Subaru Forester SJ (2013-2018), Subaru Legacy BN (2014-2019), Subaru Outback BS (2014-present), Subaru Exiga YA (2012-2015) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Port injection. Compression ratio: 10.3:1 (increased from FB25A). Power: 173 hp (129 kW) at 5,800 rpm, 235 Nm at 4,000 rpm. Dual AVCS. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Oil consumption is less severe than FB25A but still present. Cam carrier leaks are common on higher-mileage units. - Interchange note: Generally interchangeable with FB25A, but ECU may need reflashing. Ensure the replacement matches your transmission type (CVT vs manual). ### FB25D - 2018-present (direct injection) - Fitted to: Subaru Forester SK (2018-present), Subaru Outback BT (2020-present) - Key technical difference: Naturally aspirated, DOHC, 16-valve. Direct injection (fuel injectors directly in the cylinder head). Compression ratio: 12.0:1 (significantly higher than FB25B). Power: 182 hp (136 kW) at 5,800 rpm, 247 Nm at 3,700 rpm. Dual AVCS. Features a high-pressure fuel pump. Meets Euro 6 emissions standards. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Carbon buildup on intake valves is a concern - a known downside of direct injection. Oil consumption is less common than on earlier FB25s. The higher compression ratio makes the engine more sensitive to fuel quality. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with FB25A/B - fuel system, ECU, wiring loom, and high-pressure pump differ completely. Only replace with another FB25D. ### FB25 e-Boxer (mild hybrid) - 2020-present - Fitted to: Subaru Forester e-Boxer (some markets), Subaru Outback e-Boxer (some markets) - Key technical difference: FB25D with a mild hybrid system (12V lithium-ion battery and integrated starter-generator). The engine itself is mechanically identical to FB25D. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Same as FB25D - carbon buildup. Hybrid-specific components (battery, motor) have their own separate failure modes (not covered on this page). - Interchange note: Not a direct swap with non-hybrid FB25D without the full hybrid system.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement FB25 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used FB25 makes sense if you're replacing a high-mileage unit in a lower-value car (e.g., an early Forester or Legacy). However, be aware of oil consumption (FB25A/B) and cam carrier leaks. A used engine with documented service history and low mileage (under 60k) is a reasonable bet. Avoid early FB25A (2010-2012) with no oil consumption fix applied.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper FB25 recon addresses the known weak points: for FB25A/B, new piston rings with improved design (to solve oil consumption); for FB25D, a thorough carbon cleaning of intake valves. Both variants get new timing chain tensioner, new water pump, new cam carrier seals, and new gaskets. A 12-month warranty is standard. Reconditioned units are the sweet spot for most owners - you get reliability upgrades without a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full FB25 rebuild is justified when you own a high-value example (e.g., a well-specced Outback or later Forester) and want the engine to last another 150,000+ miles. For FB25A/B, forged pistons can be fitted to eliminate oil consumption permanently. For FB25D, a rebuild includes new valve guides and seals to reduce carbon buildup. Budget £3,500-£5,000 for a quality rebuild.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The FB25 sits in mid-to-large Subaru models - Forester values range from £5,000-£25,000; Outback £6,000-£28,000; Legacy £4,000-£15,000 depending on year and mileage. A reconditioned FB25 at £2,200-£3,500 represents 15-50% of vehicle value - generally viable for most examples. For a high-mileage (£4,000-£6,000) early Forester or Legacy, a full rebuild at £5,000 may approach or exceed vehicle value - evaluate the car's overall condition before committing. .

items.question: How much does a Subaru FB25 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned FB25 supply-only costs £2,200-£3,500, with fitted prices from £3,100-£4,400. Used units start from £1,500 supply-only. Rebuilt engines cost £3,500-£5,000 supply-only.

items.question: What are the most common FB25 engine problems?
items.answer: The FB25 suffers from oil consumption (FB25A/B, especially 2010-2018), cam carrier and valve cover leaks (80k-150k miles), and cooling system failures. Oil consumption can require a short block replacement or full rebuild (£2,500-£4,000). Cam carrier resealing costs £800-£1,500. Valve cover gaskets cost £300-£600. The FB25 does NOT have the EJ25's notorious head gasket failure issue.

items.question: Which Subaru models use the FB25 engine?
items.answer: The FB25 is fitted to the Subaru Forester (2010-present), Subaru Legacy (2012-2019), Subaru Outback (2012-present), and Subaru Exiga (2012-2015) in the UK. The FB25A/B is in pre-2018 models with port injection. The FB25D is in 2018+ models with direct injection.
bullets: The FB25A/B is in pre‑2018 models with port injection.
The FB25D is in 2018+ models with direct injection.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned FB25?
items.answer: A reconditioned FB25 is the safer choice - it includes improved piston rings (for oil consumption on FB25A/B) and new cam carrier seals, plus a 12-month warranty. Used FB25s are acceptable if low-mileage and with service history. Avoid early FB25A (2010-2012) without oil consumption fix.
bullets: Used FB25s are acceptable if low‑mileage and with service history.
Avoid early FB25A (2010-2012) without oil consumption fix.

items.question: What's the difference between FB25 and EJ25?
items.answer: The FB25 replaces the EJ25 - it has a timing chain (no belt replacement), dual AVCS, and significantly lower head gasket failure rates. The FB25 is more fuel-efficient and quieter, but early FB25A/B units suffered oil consumption issues. The FB25 is more modern but not a direct swap into an EJ25 car.
bullets: The FB25 is more modern but not a direct swap into an EJ25 car.

items.question: How long does an FB25 engine last?
items.answer: With regular maintenance (oil changes every 6k miles), an FB25 can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. Oil consumption may appear around 60k-120k miles on earlier units. Cam carrier leaks may require attention around 80k-150k miles. The FB25 is generally more durable than the EJ25 it replaced.
